# SE worker-speed provider admission fixture

This disposable F200/Space Exploration `0.7.57` fixture declares one reviewed finite prerequisite closure and has four versioned roles under its single mod identity. It is host-controlled fixture apparatus, not a player source, migration, graph solver, or release artifact.

| Role | Fixture | MIR | Cap | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `0.1.0` | `5.0.20015` | 0 | Validates the fixed 196-row finite declaration before direct ordered source grants, then records actual per-force rows. |
| `admission` | `0.2.1` | `5.0.20015` | 0 | Reads the source through a real configuration callback, records its starting game tick, holds unchanged public frames until at least two elapsed ticks, and writes one owned admission save. |
| `old` | `0.3.0` | `5.0.20015` | 10 | A passive expected-old opponent that records the retained source before stopping. |
| `candidate` | `0.4.0` | `5.0.20018` | 10 | Requires admitted provenance and all recorded rows before its single ordinary level-ten completion, save, and cold reads. |

`prerequisites.lua` is the explicit fixed closure captured offline from accepted data-stage raw input `AB6B409DAC6FED18DDE74461311BCDB33FAEAD9AA6CB9138E6349A20B3FB67BE`. It is a static ordered declaration with exact direct parents; runtime code neither discovers ancestors nor invokes recursive research, research-all, or a fallback closure.

Only `source` writes the declared prerequisite research state. Admission reads and compares actual public rows, flags, current research, queue, exact zero saved progress, and bonuses without repairing them. The source records player level ten at 27% with two tail entries, an unrelated fixture-native foreign research at 42%, and an idle earned level thirteen frame. Runtime treats the infinite target maximum as `4294967295`; the data-stage contract separately retains the authored `"infinite"` value. Runtime unit costs are explicitly checked as level 10/11/13 counts `3200`/`6400`/`25600` at `3600` ticks, with the eight one-count science names treated as a set. The candidate admits only the product-normalized single player tail entry and the literal cap projection: player remains enabled/hidden at level ten, while above-cap foreign and earned rows are disabled/visible. It still binds all 196 finite rows, current work, queues, bonuses, and exact zero saved progress before any fixture metadata or lab is written.

The candidate records a non-scripted level-ten completion observed at level eleven, refuses any level-eleven start or queued continuation, and refills each actual lab stack in bounded 200-item requests while recording accepted counts. The 3200-unit target with 27% pre-work progress requires 2336 consumed units per science, while a positive remainder must remain after completion. Admission and candidate holds record their starting game tick and save only after at least two elapsed ticks, so a same-tick first callback cannot satisfy the hold. The candidate then saves once and makes cold reads through local load flags only. A configuration callback clears a preceding local cold flag only after its event and source checks succeed, so a genuine cold-only load remains read-only. Candidate marker bodies project only plain frames, events, feed counts, closed state, and scalar lab validity/name/unit/disabled/inventory observations; the persisted lab entity stays out of emitted JSON. Its markers are `source`, `admission-pre-hold`, `admission-saved`, `admission-cold`, `old-opponent`, `candidate-pre-work`, `candidate-complete`, and `candidate-cold` beneath `script-output/se-worker-speed-provider/`.

Host controls are implementation checks only. They do not prove that Space Exploration admits the source configuration, that MIR15/MIR18 applies the assumed queue normalization, that a native save transitions safely, or that any historical/candidate/release scenario is qualified. Those require separately frozen package/controller inputs and native source, admission, old-opponent, candidate-completion, save, and cold evidence.
